age_display: 5- and 6-year rye blend + 10 months in separate rum casks (2022)
grain: Blend of 5- and 6-year straight rye whiskeys from Sagamore's then-contract era; exact proportions for this bottling unverified.
grain_confidence: A matched critic attributes MGP-era whiskey to the 2022 edition, but the high/low rye recipe proportions in the final vat are not disclosed.
identity: Nationwide March 2022 Rum Cask Finish Reserve Series, 98 proof, 5- and 6-year straight ryes divided into Jamaican and South American rum casks for 10 months, then reblended. Not the 2019 one-cask distillery-exclusive rum edition.
short_version: An expressive 98-proof rum-finished rye combining molasses, dark fruit and toasted coconut with fresh herbal rye spice. Independent critics find it fun and layered, although the rum lifts off the nose faster than the palate.
production: The 2022 edition was built from separately matured 5- and 6-year-old straight rye whiskey, then transferred to Jamaican and South American rum barrels for a further ten months. It was blended back at 98 proof and released nationally, unlike the 2019 distillery-only Jamaican high-ester rum cask experiment.
finish: 10 months in distinct Jamaican and South American ex-rum casks following at least 5 years of new oak maturation; 2019 release was not the same recipe.
history: Sagamore had made a limited 2019 Jamaican rum cask whiskey at its Baltimore distillery; its reception prompted the more broadly distributed 2022 two-rum-region edition.
The March 2022 launch was a Reserve Series product, not necessarily found in present 2026 state-control retail stock.

reviews.summary: Reviews precisely identified October 2022 Batch 1A: finds the nose somewhat erratic and grassy, with pepper and wood overtaking early rum esters; praises a more deftly integrated palate of buttery sweetness, cocoa, vanilla, cherry, toast and late orange peel. The sample improved with time.
reviews.scope: 2022 98-proof Reserve Series, identified reviewer bottle Batch 1A. Not the 2019 release.

reviews.summary: Describes rich cinnamon loaf, molasses and coconut on the nose, tropical punch, coconut and starfruit on the palate, then banana and cayenne. Enthusiastic but does not provide unambiguous full publication year; identity supported by 98 proof and the two-region 10-month finish.
reviews.scope: Two-region rum-finishing version at 98 proof; archive does not show exact calendar year of sample; secondary supporting source only.

quality_rationale: Very good category-relative rye on well-attested 2022-style sensory: lively rum-sweet tropical and chocolate notes coexist with rye herb/spice. The initially unsettled nose reported for named Batch 1A and bottle variation cap confidence below a firmly excellent assessment.
quality_confidence: Medium for exact 2022 Rum Reserve identity, but the strongest critic source is specific Batch 1A; independent corroborating review does not state a full year.
evidence_limit: 2022 exact Batch 1A impressions are not necessarily the sensations in every bottle. No score or tasting is imported from the separate 2019 single-Jamaican-barrel experiment.

age_display: 4- and 6-year rye blend + 10 months in Sierra Nevada red ale casks (2020)
grain: Blend of 4- and 6-year straight rye whiskeys; precise high/low mash bill fractions are not established for this exact 2020 edition.
grain_confidence: 2020 launch describes two ages and the finishing casks, not exact rye/corn/barley component percentages.
identity: Sagamore Brewer's Select Sierra Nevada Rye Ale Barrel Finish, 2020, 90 proof: 4- and 6-year ryes rested an additional 10 months in former Sagamore rye barrels that had first been used by Sierra Nevada for rye red ale. Distinct from 98-proof Ale Cask Finish.
short_version: A lighter, distinctive 90-proof 2020 rye with herbal dill, citrus, floral and caramel notes from a Sierra Nevada red-ale-cask cycle; a matched critic finds it surprisingly fruity, sweet and pleasant.
production: The initial rye barrels traveled to Sierra Nevada where a rye-enriched red ale matured in them; returned to Sagamore, those same beer-soaked barrels held a blend of four- and six-year straight ryes for a further 10 months. Bottled at 90 proof in May 2020.
finish: 10 months in reclaimed Sierra Nevada red-ale barrels that had previously held Sagamore rye. Barrel provenance is part of the unique 2020 Brewer's Select identity.
history: The cross-industry Sagamore/Sierra Nevada partnership recycled barrel influence in both directions: red ale first into old rye casks, then finished rye whiskey back into the former ale casks.
This 2020 Brewer's Select is not the separately listed 98-proof Ale Cask Finish with a different secondary age and provenance.

reviews.summary: June 15 2020 appraisal describes a fragrant dill/herbal and flower-like nose, then a softer, tropical-citrus and sweet fruit palate with subtle ale influence, mild finish and good drinkability. Publication discloses sample might have been supplied or purchased, without claiming which.
reviews.scope: Exact 2020 90-proof Brewer's Select Rye Ale with Sierra Nevada; matched to spring 2020 launch.

quality_rationale: A good-to-very-good rye expressing a successful unusual red-ale barrel experiment: approachable floral fruit, caramel and mild grain spice. Only one exact independent long-form critic review supports the estimate, and 90 proof and short finish limit depth; clearly provisional.
quality_confidence: Low-to-medium; one matched 2020 independent review plus independently verified producer collaboration specs; no additional independently corroborated bottle-specific critic sample.
evidence_limit: Do not convert the reviewer's separate numerical scale into the project's 1–10 scale. Do not assume 98-proof Ale Cask is the same bottle or claim wide contemporary availability.

age_display: Four-year straight rye + 7 months in pinot noir, shiraz and port casks (2018)
grain: Blend of straight rye whiskeys used for the 2018 limited release; precise mash bill percentages unpublished for this bottling.
grain_confidence: Producer details original 4-year maturation and 7-month finishing, but not exact proportions of high- and low-rye components.
identity: Sagamore Reserve Vintner's Finish Rye, spring 2018 Maryland/DC-only edition, 98.4 proof and 7 months in different pinot noir, shiraz, and port casks after four years in new oak. Different from 2019/2023 Port Finish rye.
short_version: A 98.4-proof limited 2018 rye with dark cherry, spiced red wine, cocoa and dry wood notes supported by matched independent tasting. No trustworthy 2018 bottle-size-specific USD price has been verified, so Value and Overall remain N/A.
production: The early Sagamore finishing experiment used a four-year straight rye blend, separately rested in pinot noir, shiraz and port casks for seven months, and reblended before bottling at a documented 98.4 proof. The 2018 public release targeted Maryland and Washington DC.
finish: Seven months in three separate red-wine and fortified-wine cask styles: pinot noir, shiraz, port; do not confuse with Port Finish rye.
history: Released as a limited 2018 reserve project shortly after Sagamore's Baltimore distillery opened, when sourced rye still underpinned much of the brand.
One contemporaneous release article rounded the proof to 98, but the producer and matched Distiller identity both list 98.4; preserve exact 98.4 specification.

reviews.summary: Independent expert record notes tart cherry and green apple on the nose, then wine, mulled spices, cocoa-rich cherries, butterscotch and dry oak on the palate. Describes a peppery medium-length finish with woody/tannic cedar aspects.
reviews.scope: Exact 2018 Vintner's Finish, 98.4 proof, limited Maryland/DC edition.

reviews.summary: 2018 double-gold tasting assessment reports layered brown sugar, apricot and cocoa with woody and peppery spice; competition panel is not treated as an independent second first-person bottle reviewer.
reviews.scope: 2018 competition category includes Sagamore Vintner's 98.4 proof, supporting historical identity and general flavor direction.

quality_rationale: Provisional very good rye: matched independent critic finds convincing sour cherry, dried wine fruit and spice layers, with mild tannic/dryness limitations. A second 2018 judging source corroborates style, but the evidence does not establish exceptional integration or justify a higher precise score.
quality_confidence: Low-to-medium; one exact independent expert sensory record and a 2018 tasting panel, with no authenticated release-specific current availability.
evidence_limit: Historical press wording rounds proof to 98; use producer-confirmed 98.4. The Fifty Best award is a judging context, not proof of universal preference.
